newsitem.title: USA: Key witnesses recant in U.S. death penalty case.
newsitem.headline: Key witnesses recant in U.S. death penalty case.

text.p: Efforts to save convicted murderer Coleman Wayne Gray from execution in Virginia next week took a new twist Wednesday as three key witnesses recanted testimony that led a jury to impose the death penalty on Gray 11 years ago.

In affadavits given to Gray's lawyers, co-defendant Melvin Tucker and two other witnesses said they lied under pressure from police and prosecutor C. Phillips Ferguson. Ferguson was not immediately available for comment.

Gray, 39, is scheduled to die next Wednesday for the May 1985 murder of grocery store manager Richard McClelland. He was convicted in Suffolk County Court in southern Virginia largely on the testimony of Tucker, who made a deal with the prosecution to avoid the death penalty himself.

Tucker testified that Gray shot McClelland to death, testimony he still sticks to today, but he also testified in the penalty phase of the trial that Gray told him he had also killed Lisa Sorrell, and her three-year-old daughter, Shanta, in 1984, in much the same way he murdered McClelland.
The other witnesses, who were in jail with Gray at the time of the trial, also recanted testimony that they heard Gray boast of the Sorrell murder.
Although no one had ever been accused of killing the Sorrells, prosecutors used that alleged admission to convince an all-white jury to order Gray's execution.
Gray's attorneys have appealed to the U.S. Court of Appeals in Richmond for a stay of execution and permission to file a new Habeus Corpus petition.

"A state prosecutor knowingly presented false testimony from several witnesses, including Melvin Tucker, a co-defendant who was committed to perjuring himself and this perjurer's false testimony was the linchpin of the state's case," the defence petition says.
The court has asked the Commonwealth of Virginia to respond to the defence petition by Thursday.
Don Harrison, a spokesman in the office of the Virginia Attorney General, said there would be no comment until the state had filed its response with the court.

Both McClelland and Lisa Sorrell were shot in the head six times with the same kind of gun. In both cases, the murderer set the victim's car on fire after the killing. But Gray was never charged with the Sorrell murders.
The evidence about the Sorrells surprised the defence and helped the prosecution secure the death penalty for Gray.
In his affadavit, Tucker now admits that he lied. "I never heard Coleman Gray say anything about the Sorrell woman and child," he said.

"The story I gave about Gray looking in the newspaper and referring to a picture of the Sorrells was a lie. My testimony concerning Coleman Gray telling me that he killed the Sorrell woman and child was a lie.

"I never heard about the Sorrells until I was in Mr. Ferguson's office. Ferguson wanted me to testify that Gray admitted killing the Sorrells. .... (He) knew I was not testifying truthfully about the Sorrell murder," Tucker added.
Ferguson was not immediately available for comment. But in an interview with Reuters last week he said he was convinced Gray had killed the Sorrells.
"I felt Gray was the murderer of the Sorrells. But that was just one portion of the evidence of a big picture relating to Gray's future dangerousness to society," he said.

The defence petition also includes affadavits from two other witnesses, Larabee Bryan Ferrell and Keith Earl Godwin, both of whom now say their testimony at the original trial that Gray had bragged about killing the Sorrells was a lie.
"I was coerced into providing this false testimony ... I met with Mr. Ferguson to discuss my testimony before I took the witness stand," said Ferrell.
Legal experts said the Fourth Circuit Court was the most conservative in the nation and Gray still faced an uphill task in having his execution stayed.

If this appeal fails, he can still turn to a U.S. Supreme Court that has already rejected his appeal once and with a bid for clemency to Virginia Gov. George Allen, who has stopped only one execution since 1994 while allowing 15 others to proceed.
